title: Arnold soccer sports gold theme for monumental season - NewsBreak
text:
By Karli Koskovich ,
51 minutes ago
PANAMA CITY BEACH, Fla. (WMBB) – The Arnold boys soccer program is aiming to secure a third consecutive state title after winning back-to-back in 2023 and 2024; the team is also introducing a new kit for 2025.
The Marlins enter the year with a new look, adding gold detailing to their uniforms, (including gold numbers, trim and a redesigned crest) symbolizing the standard set under head coach Jona Hammond.
Hammond is entering his tenth season leading the program. The color pays tribute to nine district titles, five regional championships, three state crowns and a MaxPreps national championship earned throughout his tenure.
“We kind of have a gold theme this year,” Hammond said. “We believe we’ve created the gold standard for soccer programs on the boys side, maybe even the girls side, in the panhandle.”
Players said the gold is more than a color change, it is a reminder of the expectations that come with wearing the jersey.
Arnold’s rise to national recognition has been built on routine, preparation and commitment. Players say the team treats soccer as a full-time responsibility.
“Sometimes watch we film for like an hour and a half and then practice after. Sometimes it’s the other way around, but it’s a lot.” senior Demarco Perez said.
“It’s our life,” senior Nolan Kavouras said. “We’re together six days a week. We see each other more than our families. Other teams don’t have the commitment we have.”
The Marlins won each of their last two state titles through penalty shootouts, an outcome the players say was no accident.
“We spent a lot of time on those, and it paid off,” senior Zach Wickard said, emphasizing on the attention to detail by Coach Hammond.
Hammond said the program’s internal expectations are just as demanding as the ones placed on them from outside.
“It’s hard to play against us, but it’s even harder to play for us,” Hammond said. “We’re going to put the time in, film, training, scouting, whatever it takes to be prepared.”
Only a few programs in Florida high school boys soccer history have achieved a state title three-peat.
None have ever won four straight.
Arnold hopes to add its name to that short list this season, while setting its sights on making history beyond that.
The Marlins open regular-season play at home against the North Bay Haven Buccaneers on Friday, Nov. 7.
